method: One fresh agent session per task drives Atelier, loading the atelier-sprite skill and working only through Atelier's tools in its own isolated store. Every model draws the same ten tasks from identical frozen briefs (showcase/tasks/*.txt). The Anthropic models run in headless Claude Code (claude -p) with customizations and MCP servers disabled and only the Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, and Grep tools available; the OpenAI models run in Codex. Reasoning effort: every model is tested at xhigh. The eight Anthropic sets and gpt-6-astra-xhigh ran at xhigh; gpt-5.6-sol-max and gpt-6.1-sol-max ran at max, are not directly comparable, and will be re-run at xhigh as access allows. For Claude Code the effort is the level requested on the command line and every assistant turn was checked for the requested model; for gpt-6.1-sol-max all session turns were checked for the requested model and effort. Counts: a CLI wrapper records every Atelier call, including failed calls and excluding harness export and verification, for every set except gpt-5.6-sol-max, whose agents self-reported their tool-call and doc_look tallies. Tokens are cumulative input plus output from the session's reported usage, including cached input (and cache writes for Claude Code); these runs also record the separate token-usage fields. Per-agent tokens are unavailable for gpt-5.6-sol-max and gpt-6-astra-xhigh and remain null. Durations are omitted: agents ran concurrently, so wall-clock is queueing, not work. Interrupted sessions were resumed with their original stores and artwork. Five Claude Code sessions (sonnet-5-xhigh/potion, sonnet-5-xhigh/slash, opus-4.8-xhigh/slash, opus-5-xhigh/person, opus-5-xhigh/potion) were killed by a host restart before reporting usage; their input tokens are summed from per-message usage and their output tokens cover only the resumed invocation, so those totals slightly undercount. The same restart corrupted a few bytes of the sonnet-5-xhigh/potion call log, so its call count may be short by one.
server: The 10 gpt-5.6-sol-max runs used atelier 1.7.0 through isolated in-process CLI dispatch. Later builds require 32-bit integers where earlier builds silently accepted fractions, so the gpt-5.6-sol-max/slash replay had 5 fractional arguments rounded to integers and its GIF regenerated; the calls are otherwise the model's own. This changed under 1% of that animation's pixels. The 10 gpt-6-astra-xhigh runs used the repository build at 2c1ec81c837b390f23f433c2502e5704bda7c23e (reported version 0.1.0, 25-tool surface). The 10 gpt-6.1-sol-max runs used the repository build at 225b07cda54688473df7c0310c59e1ee00ce4eb2 (reported version 0.1.0, 25-tool surface) with codex-cli 0.159.2. The 80 Anthropic runs used one binary built from the repository at ac90b5d6f096876776da670e7cd868c40012d354 (reported version 0.1.0, 26-tool surface) with Claude Code 2.1.295 or 2.1.296. Every run used isolated CLI dispatch with one store per task. All 110 replays were verified against the ac90b5d build.
verified: Every GIF parsed from disk: all 110 are 10 frames x 100ms = 1000ms, 32x32 (48x48 for beam) at scale 4, within the requested colour limits and with transparency. CI replays all 110 committed JSONL files through the repository build and requires the exported GIFs to match byte-for-byte.
